#6760. Are Young Men the New Kings of the Swing Vote?

Two years ago, it seemed that the young men of Gen Z were shaping up to be hardcore conservatives. More than half of them voted for Donald Trump’s second presidency, refuting the idea that young people tend to lean progressive. Liberal media panicked about finding “a Joe Rogan of the left” who could reach them, and conservatives took a victory lap. “Gen Z Has Turned Right!” Fox News’s Greg Gutfeld announced, citing a report from the Harvard Kennedy School that highlighted, among other insights, the ways social media has led to an increase in conservatism among young folks. A Turning Point USA Poll from around the same time declared Generation Z “the most conservative generation in decades.”

On Tuesday night, though, as a blue tidal wave flipped states from Iowa to Texas, it was young men who comprised a critical segment of the new Democratic coalition. As reported by CIRCLE, a non-partisan research organization at Tufts University, white men between the ages of 18 to 29 voted blue by a 10-point margin; in 2024, exit polling indicated that 56% of all young men voted for Donald Trump. Even more remarkably, young people across the board voted for Democratic congressional candidates by a 40% margin, according to data from NBC.

“In the wake of 2024, there was this whole catastrophizing panic,” says Aidan Kohn-Murphy, the founder of Gen Z for Change (formerly known as TikTok for Biden) and a prominent political influencer. “Oh my God, everything we thought about Gen Z is wrong. It's actually a conservative generation. And no, that's not what was happening. I mean, a huge part of Gen Z just didn't show up to vote because they didn't feel like they had a reason.”

For Democratic strategist Eric Stern, connecting with men on an emotional level was critical in getting them out to vote. Stern has worked on Ruben Gallego and John Fetterman’s campaigns; his political ad agency, FIGHT, has produced spots for Mayor Zohran Mamdani, Senator-Elect Abdul El-Sayed, and Governor-Elect Gina Hinojosa, to name a few. This election cycle, Stern sought to change voters’ perception of what a Democrat can look like.

“Our most notable ad of the general election was Bob [Brooks] standing in front of a literal dumpster fire and then putting it out because he's a firefighter,” he said. Brooks, now the Representative-elect in the Lehigh Valley, flipped his seat on Tuesday. “A ton of Latino men are really into boxing and MMA fighting, and so Ruben [Gallego] held events around boxing,” Stern told me. For Texas’ Hinojosa, who'll become the state’s first Democratic governor in 35 years when she's sworn in in January, that meant running an ad during Mexican boxing champion Canelo Álvarez's match against Christian Mbilli, an event with a massive Latino viewing audience.

Still, Kohn-Murphy and Stern both argued that the main issue on the ballot this cycle was affordability. “If you look at polling, far and away the top issue for voters is cost of living,” Stern said. “And so you can run a million ads saying that ‘Jane Doe is for they/them,’ but it's not going to resonate with people in the same way if they can't afford to keep their lights on.”

When I asked Republican political consultant Kirsten Kukowski about young men voting blue, she brought up affordability too. After all, nearly nine months into the Iran War, a barrel of oil still costs $100. “Men and young men voted with their bank accounts,” she offered. “And for the last several years, that's how they've been voting. And I think that's how Donald Trump won that group two years ago, because he was talking about affordability and inflation.”

Kukowski, the former Communications Director for the Republican National Committee, now runs her own firm, K2 and Company, out of Minneapolis. “At some point here, people expect results,” she continued. “People expected results from Donald Trump, and they didn't see that. So now we're on the clock again for another two years.”

#6758. With the Hunger Games Press Tour, Have We Reached the Final Frontier of Method Dressing?

The cast has offered a pointed take on the state of today’s red carpets

Another Hunger Games movie, a prequel to the initial series, premieres later this month, and with it comes another press tour full of fantastically far-fetched fashion. As the promotional events begin to stack up for Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, we are reminded of the familiar lore of this dystopian empire: In a fictionalized future America called Panem, the 12 districts that supply resources to the rich and powerful people of the Capitol are forced to send two children to fight to the death each year. The excess of the Capitol is signaled in the films via outlandish style, which the newest film’s cast members have been attempting to channel in their recent looks. The goal is to be extreme—but in an era of extremes on the red carpet, these over-the-top ensembles actually don’t look so out of place.

Elle Fanning plays a young Effie Trinket, who is essentially a Capitol stylist dressing the young “tributes” in all sorts of fanciful fashions—and doing the same for herself. (In the first film series, the character wore a lot of McQueen.) So far, Fanning’s press looks have deliberately channeled that outlandishness. For a London fan screening, she wore a gown from Robert Wun’s Fall 2026 couture collection that subverted ideas of childlike wonder. Her ensemble began in miniature with a music-box-style ballerina atop a bubblegum pink fascinator. The corresponding human-size gown features a doubled-up bodice, the outer layer appearing to peel off, above a full tulle skirt, all in that same dusty pink.

For her other appearances, Fanning has established a de facto uniform of precisely tailored skirt suits, each paired with some sort of coordinating fascinator tilted just so above her brow. She has selected a soft pink pleated skirt suit from Valentino complete with a ruffled collar, gloves, and a butterfly-trimmed chapeau; a sharp-shouldered version in a deep, almost reptilian satin green from Demna’s Gucci; and a floral, bow-embellished one from Vivienne Westwood. The looks are decidedly feminine in a manner that is at once both futuristic and retro in very Capitol fashion.

Fanning’s stylist Samantha McMillen has been vocal about the references to the character, with captions like “Gucci Effie | @demna puts “The Hunger” into @thehungergames,” and “Elle bringing 🦋 “Sunrise” 🦋 to the Academy Gala.” And it’s not just Fanning doing this either. Costar Mckenna Grace recently recreated a Katniss Everdeen Capitol tour look in which Katniss’s dress quite literally caught fire. Created by Vietnamese designer Cong Tri, who is known for his sculptural silhouettes, the recreation nixed the pyrotechnics but printed graphic flames onto the skirt and bodice. With the help of stylist Molly Dickson, Grace also revived Katniss’s wedding dress with a frothy white, silver-embellished gown by Monique Lhuillier.

I haven’t seen the most recent films, but all of them examine the same concept of this dystopian society propped up by the Hunger Games themselves at different points on a timeline. In the first film specifically, the older Trinket uses their version of a press tour to craft a narrative around Katniss and her fellow tribute Peeta Mellark and win favor among their audience through larger-than-life fashion. The aforementioned fire dress referenced Everdeen’s district’s coal mining industry, and the wedding dress was meant to create the illusion of a love story between the two of them. The series of looks is designed to be projected to the surrounding communities—and garner as much attention as possible. The characters can quite literally benefit later in the life-and-death-style games from the loyalties and sympathies the theatrics spawn.

It’s only in recent years that this idea of method dressing, or theming press tour looks around an actor’s current project, has become commonplace. It began in earnest with the work of Law Roach and Zendaya around the Dune and Spider-Man franchises, Challengers, and The Drama. It was perhaps commercially crystallized in 2023 by Andrew Mukamal and Margot Robbie with Barbie—a press tour that spawned so much digital attention it earned its own coffee-table book—and, more recently, Wuthering Heights. Now, it has proof of concept, attracting stars like Cynthia Erivo and Ariana Grande in their promotion of Wicked, the new cast of Sense and Sensibility, and Lili Reinhart’s rom-com references for The Love Hypothesis. At its most reductive, the tactic is a surefire way to drum up conversation on social media; at its best, a clever way to add depth to a project’s storytelling.

As press tours become more and more oriented towards social media, it’s difficult to isolate the influence of method dressing on the red carpet’s current proclivity towards extremes. Everyone is trying to capitalize on the sort of hype that the Met Gala ensembles can drum up. Your reference needs to be loud enough to cut through the noise—pyrotechnics optional. It’s perhaps why avant-garde, couture, and couture-level designers like Wun, who dressed a large handful of stars at this year’s Met Gala, are carving out more and more space among these sorts of promotional events. At the same time, brands like Standing Ground and Matieres Fecales—it’s only a matter of time before Fanning wears one of those skirt suits—are also gaining traction as stylists treat the red carpet more like a magazine editorial than an occasion to get dressed up.

Then last night, Grace added another layer. She and Dickson have begun to look outside the films to reference looks of Jennifer Lawrence’s own. Lawrence played Katniss in the first movies. For a Madrid premiere, she wore a Miss Sohee couture dress that paid homage to the Givenchy naked dress Lawrence wore for this year’s Golden Globes. It all feels very meta, calling into question the role of fashion in these promotional spaces, real or fictional. On the IRL Hunger Games red carpet, the reference is dystopian extravagance—but with the rise of method dressing and the corresponding celebration of larger, louder looks, has dystopian extravagance already become the norm? In this case, it may not be life and death, but it could make or break your movie.

Arjona’s recent work in Onslaught, where she plays an army veteran and single mother with PTSD, has expanded her range, and she’ll next appear in The Thomas Crown Affair in March. Away from the set, the Puerto Rican actress has made community work a long-standing commitment, supporting underserved women in downtown Los Angeles for more than a decade and children in Guatemala for 15 years.

From her beauty routine to the final look, plus a car ride filled with friends and family, Arjona brought ELLE behind the scenes as she prepared for the Chateau Marmont celebration.

#6756. 13 Rugby Shirts Under $150 for Credible Old-Money Cosplay

Historically, rugby shirts are a somewhat conflicted character in the never-ending tale of menswear shirting. On one hand, they’re a prep staple on par with OCBDs, loafers, and boat shoes. On the other hand, they were quite literally designed to handle the rigors of full-contact rugby and were later embraced by folks who proudly call themselves dirtbags.

There’s an interesting duality to rugby shirts: they can feel twee or they can feel traditionally sporty. Thanks to this polarity, it makes it even easier to fit into your wardrobe. Regardless of which camp you fall in, rugby’s crush. And thanks to a recent resurgence, we thought it would be a good idea to highlight some rugby shirts under $150.

Not only are they traditionally as comfortable as any polo you own, they’re also refined enough to take into stuffier settings, rugged enough to handle some serious outdoor exploration and flexible enough to wear from Friday to Monday morning (but don’t do that, probably). And while we love an expensive version of, well, anything, we also love it when we can find some killer alternatives for prices we’d like to think of as reasonable. There wasn’t a paucity of options either, so we rounded up 13 of our favorites, right below.

One of the least expensive options on this list is also one of the best—the loose, shorter cut makes wearing it with jeans, some chinos or virtually anything else in your closet as easy as any polo you have in the arsenal.

J.Crew has a few louder options in the catalog, but the pared-down, solid-bodied iterations are even more affordable and play a supporting role with as much skill and charisma as your favorite character actor.

There is an actual science to color combinations, and Gramicci deserves an Einstein Award for this one.

When done right, a rugby can be one of the best outdoors shirts on the market, and this one is just that: super comfortable, a little hardy and delightfully reminiscent of the ones you would've seen in Camp 4.

There's simply no way that the company founded by an original Camp 4 denizen could ever make a rugby not worthy of a Half Dome assault, and it's also improbably still under $150.

Alex Mill makes a few killer monochromatic, garment-dyed variations of this striped number, but this one is more fun than those and we could all use a little bit of fun when the days are as short as they are now.

It's odd to call something a rugby if it doesn't have a contrasting placket, but this one gets a pass because everything else checks out and it's also made out of a hardy-ass jersey fabric.

One of the best rugby shirts we've found also happens to meet the rigorous price qualifications of this list—and now it's half-off—and it's not all that often that the best of anything is also a value play.

Putting "Iconic" in the name is one of those things that can backfire on you if it doesn't live up to the billing, but this one does and remains both a standard of the genre and, against all odds, under $150.

Very few brands appreciate the rugby—or the possibilities that exist under the rugby banner— more than 18 East, and not only is the Harold reimagining the notion of stripe spacing within the genre, but it's also the only short-sleeve option on this list.

This one is going to keep working its way into lists as long as its available because sometimes a brand just nails it. In this case, the cocktail of perfectly-faded brown and black is radiating Leatherheads (complimentary) and the cut is the comfy kind that can layer on either side.

Some big ol' stripes, a woven collar and a cool little oxford cloth hit at the inside of the neck are just a few details elevating this one from "not bad" to "oh hell yeah." (It's also on sale, which always helps.)

Hear me out: I've made a habit of finding stuff in the women's section that fits better than anything on the men's side, and this rugby has all the trademark elements of those past hitters. Also, it might be the softest one on this whole list.

#6753. Going Home—A Day in the Life With Libby Taverner As She Walks the Chanel Show in Sydney

One of Australia’s buzziest models, Libby Taverner made her runway debut during the fall 2025 season. Since then, her career has been a frenetic blur. For spring 2027, she walked no fewer than 27 shows, Matthieu Blazy’s Chanel among them. When the storied French house decided to reprise its resort 2027 show in Sydney, it was no surprise the 20-year-old was given a ring.

The Sydney show not only marked a significant moment for Chanel—it was their first Australian outing since 1982—but also for the young model. “It’s still relatively early in my journey of living overseas. Being able to come home and walk a Chanel show in Australia feels incredibly special, and it’s an opportunity that I honestly didn’t imagine would come around so soon,” she told Vogue.

“There’s just a little sparkle in my heart knowing that I’m doing something so incredible in my home country. It makes me feel really proud,” she added.

For Taverner, the show meant that she could serve as a guide to her fellow model friends and industry peers, many of whom were experiencing their first times Down Under. Lucky for them, Taverner considers herself an expert at all things Australia, as she grew up in multiple parts of the country. “I was born in Gladstone, Queensland, before my family decided to travel around Australia,” she says. “We spent a couple of years in Perth and Bundaberg too.”

Her top Sydney recommendation? Hitting the Australian coastline. “There’s something for everyone, whether you want to swim, surf, or go for a coastal walk, or simply spend some time relaxing in the sun.” Catching the sunset at the beach with some fish and chips or and a pitstop at Yo-Chi for some fro-yo are must-dos too. “It’s such a simple thing, but to me it’s a very quintessential Australian experience.”

But most importantly for those wanting the full Aussie experience, Taverner recommends taking a step back and slowing down. “The best way to experience Australia is to slow down, explore a little, and embrace that relaxed outdoor lifestyle that we’re so lucky to have.”

Below, a day in the life of Libby Taverner as she gets ready to walk the Chanel resort 2027 reprise show in Sydney.

Fashion week is always such an exciting whirlwind, with everyone traveling from different parts of the world and moving from one city to the next. But there’s something different about walking in Sydney. It feels a little more personal, and I think there’s an added sense of gratitude because I get to experience this moment somewhere that means so much to me. It’s a feeling I don't think I’ll forget anytime soon.

#6752. Grandmacore Bags Are the Textural Treat Your Winter Wardrobe Needs

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Gather your crochet hooks and embroidery hoops and get ready to embrace fashion’s new era of cozy bags. Needlepoint, embroidery, and tapestry are taking over bags far and wide, from chic clutches to big, oversize carryalls, useful totes, and reimagined duffles. The trend kicked off about a year ago when Valentino launched its DeVain bag in November 2025 as part of its pre-fall 2026 collection under Alessandro Michele. With its beaded details, tapestry textiles, and embroidery, the bag is a love letter to a new kind of grandmacore with a dash of boho.

Much like the tassels that we’ve been seeing so much of lately, the grandmacore bag speaks volumes about tactile, touchable joy in an increasingly digital world. It’s reminiscent of a comfy couch with pillows, or a well-worn blanket that’s been passed down by generations. It’s instant, wearable craft.

Valentino isn’t the only one putting a focus on crafty, comfy bags. Just look at Dries Van Noten. One bag from the fall/winter 2026 collection in particular feels perfectly primed for the grandma-centric fashion universe: an east-west duffel-style tote replete with floral tapestry and a large snakeskin-effect patch. It feels like a wearable textural wonder with an inherent vintage sentiment; something that could have been picked up on travels in a foreign land decades ago and passed down through generations.

Elsewhere, Fendi recently reissued 20 archival versions of the Baguette under chief creative officer Maria Grazia Chiuri, most of them collaged in craft. Think: intense zebra-striped beadwork, mirror appliqué, and floral embroidery made by (and inspired by) South Asian craft. The mirror bag, for example, involves 138 hours of handwork with the Mumbai atelier Chanakya International. All of these bags is clear nods to craft in a world where fashion (and many other things) are lightning fast.

The grandma-ification of bags comes at the perfect time, too. Beyond offering a bit of slowed-down, tactile luxury, these kinds of accessories are also the perfect touch for winter and holiday dressing. There are many ways to wear the look. Silky pouches finished with embroidery by Conner Ives or feather-trimmed shoulder bags from Erdem included. Details like fringe and tassels add extra feeling. When all you see is the coat, let the bag do the talking.

But on top of that hurdle, the couple weren’t exactly communicating their feelings well, and had very different ideas about where to live and how to manage their work/life balance. So it didn’t exactly come as a shock when Aneha turned Cam down at the altar, saying “I still believe you’re my person but I do not [say yes] today. I need more time.”

Despite saying “I don’t,” Aneha seemed very open to dating Cam and working on their relationship, even telling producers “I can’t imagine my life without him.” Meanwhile, the pair had a whole convo about taking time to process where they stand and their continued love for each other, which seemed promising. But…did they stay together?

Not so much. Love Is Blind was allegedly filmed over a year ago, and according to the reunion (which was filmed recently), they are not together. Aneha revealed they’d planned a hotel retreat for after their wedding, and that during their time away Cam told her he didn’t love her and wanted to end the relationship.

Cam also revealed he was planning to say no to Aneha on their wedding day; she just happened to go first. So, guess that’s that on that! But in better news, they seem to be getting along fine as friends?

#6748. I Swear By Collagen Face Masks to Instantly Plump and Hydrate Skin

On Halloween morning, I was tidying up for a pre trick-or-treat party, hanging felt mummies and slicing a cranberry goat-cheese log. When it was time to light a moody candle in the powder room, I caught a glimpse of my reflection. I was wearing a witch hat, but the headline was my radiant skin. In Hocus Pocus, the Sanderson sisters get their glow via children’s souls, but my approach was a bit more sanguine: The night before, I’d used Sulwhasoo’s new collagen face mask before bed—and it turns out that I was right on time to incorporate one of these masks into my routine. (Not only because masks are huge on October 31.)

As we head deeper into autumn, “Our skin experiences greater transepidermal water loss, particularly as we transition between cold outdoor temperatures and heated indoor environments,” says Shannon Humphrey, MD, a board-certified cosmetic dermatologist in Vancouver. “Interestingly, it’s often during these seasonal transitions, rather than the middle of winter, that patients experience more dryness, scaling, eczema, and irritation.” Dr. Humphrey encourages patients to get ahead of these changes by incorporating richer, barrier-restoring skin-care products. “Collagen masks can be a great option for providing additional hydration and supporting the skin barrier,” she notes.

A good collagen mask can also set the stage for glowy glam at all the holiday parties to come. “I love how these masks help skin look plumper, smoother and more hydrated by morning,” says pro makeup artist Amanda Gabbard. “Foundation goes on more smoothly, fine lines look less pronounced, and you get that fresh, well-rested glow even if your actual night’s sleep was anything but restful.”

Ahead, find the collagen masks Vogue editors and skin-care experts approve of. Happy masking!

Vogue’s beauty commerce writer Concetta Ciarlo uses the Laneige Bouncy and Firm Sleeping Mask.

Vogue’s beauty commerce writer Concetta Ciarlo uses Sungboon Editor’s Deep Collagen Overnight mask.

“A collagen face mask is a treatment typically infused with collagen, peptides, and hydrating ingredients designed to nourish and plump the skin,” says Gunn, mostly available in cream or sheet formulations designed to be used before bed. “The goal is to enhance skin elasticity, hydration, and brightness while you sleep.”

Yes, they really work—but not in the way you might think. “Collagen face masks offer temporary benefits, helping to hydrate, plump the skin, reduce fine lines, and improve texture,” says Dr. Spearman. However, she continues that collagen molecules can be too large to penetrate into the skin and remain on the surface when applied. “The collagen itself may not directly penetrate deeply into the skin, but the added peptides, humectants, and antioxidants will,” Gunn adds. “These added ingredients support collagen production for a more firm appearance over time.” To do so, per Spearman, you’re best to look for ingredients like retinoids, peptides, and vitamin C.

No, collagen molecules are too large to penetrate into the skin; rather, they sit on the surface. “However, collagen peptides are often smaller, making it easier for collagen to penetrate more effectively,” says Dr. Spearman.

The benefits of collagen masks are many. “Collagen face masks hydrate, temporarily plump fine lines, and enhance skin elasticity,” according to Dr. Spearman, which can help improve overall skin texture via hydration. “In addition, hydrated skin looks smoother and firmer.”

How often should you do a collagen face mask?

Experts say that how often you use a collagen face mask is dependent on your skin type. “It is generally recommended to use a collagen face mask one to two times per week, giving your skin enough time to recover and utilize the benefits of the product,” Dr. Spearman advises. “If you have dry skin, you may use a mask two to three times per week for added moisture.”

Is it better to use a sheet or jelly/cream collagen mask?

According to Dr. Spearman, the type of mask you use is dependent on your skin type. For dry skin, jelly or cream masks are better, while sheet masks are better for oily or acne-prone skin. “Sheet collagen masks are easy to apply and remove, making them a quick and convenient option,” she continues. “The mask is designed to fit your face, ensuring an even distribution of collagen and other ingredients. Sheet masks are packaged with hydrating ingredients, providing a great amount of moisture for the skin. However, they tend to offer short-term results and may not be suitable for all skin types. On the other hand, jelly or cream collagen masks may provide deeper hydration and longer-lasting moisture,” Dr. Spearman says.

“Collagen masks are beneficial for anyone looking to improve skin hydration, firmness, and elasticity, especially those with dry, mature, or dull skin,” says Gunn; though, they’re also great for a quick dewy glow before a special occasion.

What skin concerns are collagen face masks best for?

According to Mieloch, not all collagen masks are created equally. High-end versions can deliver more dramatic results, offering real plumping, deep hydration and that post-facial smoothness. They are especially effective for mature, dehydrated, stressed or jet-lagged skin. “Then there are the individually wrapped collagen masks, the quick-fix heroes,” she says. “They’re great on the go, perfect for flights and instantly revive tired skin. Think of them as skin-care health shots.”

Are there any side effects to be aware of?

“For most skin types, a quality mask should soothe, plump, and hydrate, never irritate,” says Mieloch. The one caveat, she explains, comes from how collagen masks have blown up on TikTok. Many very young, acne-prone users are applying them every day. “That’s where I’d be careful. These masks can be a bit occlusive and may trigger congestion in breakout-prone teens.”

When we test and review a product, we take a holistic approach to deliver well-rounded product recommendations. First, we lean on Vogue’s vast network of experts—from board-certified dermatologists to celebrity estheticians—to gain professional acumen on the industry’s standout products, ones these specialists would actually use on their clients. We pair their expertise with our editorial best practices to curate the thoughtful edits you read on our site.

As it relates to collagen face masks, we selected the best based on the following characteristics: ingredients, mask type, wear time, how easily the masks stay on, and the skin-care concerns they address. To do this, we paired our own personal tests of each formula with expert guidance and reviewer insights to determine which we would recommend to you.

#6747. 7 Best Ways to Care for Gray Hair in the Colder Months, From Boosting Hydration to Restoring Shine

Easy tricks to keep silver strands healthy and hydrated when the temperature drops.

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

If red carpets and runways are anything to go by this autumn, silver strands are the trend du jour. Emma Thompson, Olivia Colman, and Sarah Jessica Parker are leading the former camp, each having debuted an elegant gray transformation in recent weeks, while shows such as Lanvin, Akrin, and Andreas Kronthaler for Vivienne Westwood spotlighted gray hair at Paris Fashion Week.

It seems, then, that there’s no better time to embrace gray and silver hair. But for anyone seeking to follow suit, it’s important to note that cooler temperatures can affect the typical upkeep involved. “Cold weather dries out gray hair, making it feel rough, brittle, and more prone to breakage and frizz,” says John Clark, senior colorist at Nicola Clarke salon. “This is because the cold, low-humidity air pulls moisture from the hair, while indoor heating further dries it out.”

Since gray hair indicates a structural change in the hair (as it’s caused by a loss of melanin in the strands), it’s often more prone to dryness, regardless of the weather. Dr. Aamna Adel, founder of Rhute Haircare, explains: “Gray or white hair often has fewer natural lipids and a rougher cuticle, which means it can feel drier and coarser. It also reflects light differently, so it can look dull or wiry.”

She adds that both the texture of the hair and the scalp can change when temperatures drop; flakiness and irritation can be common consequences.

Thankfully, there is a range of easy ways to restore both back into top form. With winter firmly on the horizon, discover the seven swaps and changes you can make to your gray hair routine to best care for it in the weeks ahead.

A healthy scalp will ensure that gray strands are stronger and denser, according to hairstylist and founder of Jo Nova, Joseph Yildiz.

Adds Dr. Adel: “Look for ceramides, fatty acids, shea butter, and panthenol to rebuild the lipid barrier; niacinamide to support scalp health; and antioxidants like vitamin E, stem cell extracts, and green tea extract to protect against oxidative stress, which accelerates graying and dryness. Amino acids and peptides can also help strengthen the hair shaft over time.”

As gray hair naturally feels coarser, the last thing you want is to strip it with shampoos that contain harsh sulfates. Opt for hydrating formulas or cleansing conditioners, and while the hair is damp, apply a leave-in conditioner.

Incorporate a silver shampoo and conditioner once a week. “It dulls any yellow or brassy tones and helps reflect the light, making hair look shiny and glossy,” says Clark.

Alongside this, a clarifying formula used once every two weeks is useful, too, especially if you tend to use a lot of styling products. “It will lightly cleanse any product buildup or mineral deposits in the hair. Sometimes white hair can appear yellow, and this solves that,” says Jo Cockle at John Frieda Salon. Always follow with a bond-building and moisturizing hair mask to keep it strong and soft.

Philip Kingsley Pure Blonde/Silver Shampoo

K18 Full-Size Leave-In Molecular Repair Hair Mask

Avoid stepping outside into the cold right after air-drying your hair. “This can be incredibly damaging to hair that is already prone to dryness. The water in your hair can expand in freezing temperatures, which can lift the hair’s cuticle and lead to split ends,” says Hollie Rose Clarke, hairstylist and Living Proof ambassador.

Instead, she recommends using a hydrating product to help keep hair soft and conditioned while air-drying. Clarke is a fan of Living Proof Air-Dry Styler, which contains hemisqualane for moisture that won’t weigh down fine strands. You can also experiment with a nourishing hair oil such as Moroccanoil’s Treatment, which is brimming with omega-6 for deep hydration.

In the evenings, Dr. Adel recommends wearing a silk or satin-lined scarf or bonnet to prevent friction and static as you sleep.

Replenish lost moisture with cocooning hair masks and treatments. Clark recommends incorporating keratin-based formulas to restore strength, while Clarke name-checks amino acids to increase hair’s hydrophobicity (this ultimately helps to lock in moisture), and hemisqualane to seal the cuticles so locks appear silkier.

Sam McKnight Hair Rich Nourish Conditioner

Ideally, try not to overstyle your hair with heated tools. “This can leave hair broken, dry, and even discolored,” says Clark. But, if you must use them (and most of us do prefer to), shield your strands with a heat protector, even if you’re just running a hair dryer through it. Look for one with hydrating, frizz-managing qualities to ease flyaways.

Wella Ultimate Smooth Miracle Hair Oil Serum

There’s a reason why some may find their grays looking lackluster. “Gray hair is more porous, meaning there is less natural protection from environmental factors (such as urban pollution) than with pigmented hair. This can be what causes a lack of shine or discoloration,” Clarke explains.

Modern shield formulas deliver hydration and protection against both heat tools and environmental damage.

Oribe Invisible Defense Universal Protection Spray

Beauty Works Solaré UV Leave-In Conditioning Mist

As a finishing touch, a small amount of hair oil will add extra shine to your grays, but a glossing treatment delivers luster that lasts. At-home glosses (which are often applied pre-conditioner or in place of it, left for a few minutes, then washed out) promise instant results. You can also use a semipermanent conditioning tint such as Shrine Drop It to revive the color of your grays.

#6746. Inside the NYC Members' Club Where Republicans and Democrats Party Together

A half-dozen of us are squeezed into a small service elevator, our various colognes clashing with the signature fish-and-rubber scent of Lower Manhattan. The elevator operator blares Chinese ballads, and the young man next to me bobs his head in appreciation. An older man shifts uncomfortably. “Could you actually make it louder?” he snarks. Over the course of one excruciatingly slow ride to the sixth floor, we’re trapped in our private discomfort or pleasure. But we’re all headed to the same place: a midterms watch party at The Bench, a members’ club for people who are into politics but feel like political outsiders. It’s a place, according to its website, where “restless organizers, creatives, misfits, sneakerheads, and policy nerds collide.”

Since its founding two years ago, The Bench has hosted insiders ranging from CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani. Monthly dues, “just to keep the lights on,” run as little as $50. The space is regularly used for events unaffiliated with The Bench: readings by literary magazines, climate week pop-ups, splashy debates. Michka Bengio, the social club’s owner and co-founder, is an earnest believer in dialogue and, if his programming is any indication, a little bit of a chaos agent. He likes to produce scenarios that underscore political tensions, like when he had Weiss’s The Free Press, co-host a watch party for Mamdani’s 2025 election. According to those who attended, it was a somber evening for the pro-Cuomo crowd, though some of them nevertheless returned to The Bench for this week’s midterms viewing.

On the night of the midterm elections, partygoers had the option of viewing the election results in a spacious, orderly room displaying CNN’s broadcast or in a lounge-y, narrower space screening Fox News’s coverage. In a cozy hallway between the two screens, guests could buy cocktails and popcorn or engage with people whose political views differ from their own—arguably The Bench’s most exclusive offering.

“There’s just a whole splatter of different opinions that come in here,” says David Azoulay, who works with the content agency Fixer Media. “The Free Press, the Manhattan Institute, and then I also get to meet a lot of people who are working in the Democratic space, on the Biden or Kamala Harris campaigns.” Azoulay helped produce events for an “America 250” tour in collaboration with Young America’s Foundation, a conservative youth organization, and has worked with provocateur Ben Shapiro and former Prime Minister Boris Johnson. Though he used to be a registered Democrat, he “grew up” and now identifies as a proud Republican. While Azoulay engaged in a playful back-and-forth with a progressive 21-year-old over what he considers to be the fallacy of socialism, Democratic councilmember Christopher Marte milled about wearing an “I Voted” sticker.

Over the sound of people screaming about the James Talarico-Ken Paxton race, Marte told me he met Bengio 10 years ago through Arena, a New York-based political organization that took off in the wake of the first Trump presidency. “It was all these young people trying to figure out how to get involved in politics. A.O.C. was on the couch, Alessandra Biaggi, all these people who were just curious, post-Trump election,” he says. At the time, Bengio was working as a campaign manager for Michael Basch, a techno-optimistic Democratic NYC mayoral candidate, a gig he secured by asking the only person he knew in politics to introduce them. He’s also worked as a consultant for NBA Africa and managed downtown restaurants like Regina’s Grocery and Miss Lily’s. The Bench is one of four Bengio ventures; he also co-founded the supper club Shtick with his wife, Jacqueline Lobel, and partners with the Hancock Foundation and the Hancock Cafe. On any given event night, he can be found buzzing around the room, excitedly facilitating introductions for his guests.

The son of a Moroccan father and Algerian mother, Bengio grew up in Strasbourg, France. When I ask what motivated him to move to New York in 2001, he deadpans: “Ever heard of the American dream?” More specifically, though, he was jealous of a friend who moved to the States for six months and returned speaking fluent English. “He was the coolest kid,” Bengio says. “And I was like, ‘I want to go to America, too.’ I love basketball,” he says, reorganizing a pile of books so that the edges aligned just so.

Bengio, a first-time voter, is coy about his own politics. Instead, he’s driven by the promise of America “that you can coexist,” he says, and a desire to nurture civil, democratic debate. “I want to be part of the project.”

“We need to really recommit and reaffirm what we mean when we talk about free speech—expression that is unencumbered by political interference in any way, shape, or form,” says Josef Palermo, a former curator at the Kennedy Center who drove up from the nation’s capital to attend this party. Earlier this year, Palermo wrote about the politicization of the Kennedy Center by both the Biden and Trump administrations in an article for The Atlantic. “We need spaces like this in D.C. Everybody’s in their own camps and certain venues are definitely coded one way or the other. I think having something like this would be huge in our nation’s capital.”

Then again, it’s partly New York’s distance from the D.C. swamp that makes talking about politics at The Bench feel cool. The space is decorated with Bengio’s enviable collection of NBA and political memorabilia. (He jokes that he stays up late scrolling vintage sites and bidding on Americana rarities.) Alongside Michael Jordan Wheaties boxes and a slew of rare basketball sneakers, there’s a framed copy of Emile Zola’s 1897 letter to the French youth during the Dreyfus affair, a portable Florida voting booth from the Bush vs. Gore election, a framed paper shift dress from Richard Nixon’s 1968 presidential campaign, and nearly every issue of John F. Kennedy Jr’s George magazine. The one with a Donald Trump cover gets taken down from the wall often, Bengio says, but he always puts it back up.

On Tuesday night, there appeared to be other collectors of rare political merch. Vintage Obama-era crop tops caught my eye, and a speechwriter for a New York City council member waxed poetic about his favorite vinyl record: a collection of John F. Kennedy speeches. Two guys wore t-shirts they designed themselves that cheekily quoted Michigan turncoat Haley Stevens: “Israel cums to me in my dreams.” (One of them requested anonymity, fearful of being cancelled by the Canary Mission, an anonymous organization that tracks critics of Israel.)

A good number of attendees who were professionally invested in the election outcomes couldn’t stop checking their phones. Anthony DiMieri, the man behind Mamdani’s winning social media strategy, told me he’d just come from Brad Lander’s party. Max Altman, the brother of the OpenAI founder Sam, also stopped by. He’s excited about a recent move to New York from Austin, Texas, and if he hadn’t forgotten to request an absentee ballot, he says, he would’ve voted for James Talarico.

As the results turned progressively blue, the room began to clear out. Before leaving, I chatted with Azoulay’s “libertarian friend” Hunt Beaty. In the hallway between broadcasts, Beaty tells me he’s not terribly moved by the midterms. “Everything interesting that is happening in the world right now, to me, is happening outside of politics,” he says. He rejects the libertarian designation and lives by the credo “free minds and free markets,” citing Reason magazine. And yet, Beaty finds that The Bench still has something to offer him.

“It’s fun to be in a room filled with buzzy, interesting people who at least are able to try and talk about ideas, while also being like, ‘Maybe we’re doing coke in the bathroom, too.’ I want there to be a New York City where those things could coexist.”

From beloved straight-leg jeans to trend-forward indigo washes and relaxed baggy cuts, these celeb-inspired denim outfits are the perfect way to rethink the perennial closet classic.

Both looks strike the perfect high-low balance, proving that denim can feel just as polished after hours as it does by day.

Whether you’re keeping things casual with wardrobe staples or dressing denim up with elevated statement pieces, the possibilities are endless. The trick is all in the styling—finding the right finishing touches to make each silhouette feel like your own.

Below, find ten celeb-inspired denim outfit ideas to give your fall wardrobe a stylish refresh.

Jennifer Lawrence loves Mom jeans, often gravitating towards the relaxed silhouette in her everyday life. While out in New York, the actress chose to wear hers with elevated basics, including an oversized navy crewneck sweater, roomy black T-shirt, and brown suede mules. A bold lime-green handbag added a vibrant unexpected pop to the otherwise understated off-duty outfit.

Sarah Pidgeon kept things classic in Rùadh’s Agnes mid-rise jeans, styling them with a white T-shirt and Aflalo’s black leather coat—repeat favorites within her wardrobe. The actress leaned into a relaxed, understated feel using other reliable go-tos, including black leather loafers and Balenciaga’s Rodeo bag. This one’s worth bookmarking to wear all season long.

Monica Barbaro embraced a classic fall formula, choosing a pair of slightly flared, wide-leg jeans as the base. The actress paired them with Me+Em’s houndstooth Pub jacket as a statement layer, along with a white crewneck T-shirt and pointy black boots. Equally suited to the office or weekend plans, grab a suede tote and minimal jewelry to round out the effortless everyday uniform.

Daisy Edgar-Jones gave subtly distressed, high-waisted blue jeans a romantic spin, pairing them with Mango’s white brocade jacket and a simple white tee while on the press tour for Sense & Sensibility. White satin pumps and a black mini shoulder bag brought the look back to the present, balancing the feminine, Regency-coded details with a more contemporary feel.

Dakota Johnson is making a case for cropped denim, stepping out multiple times in recent weeks in clean, ankle-grazing styles. The secret to giving this casual silhouette a dressier feel? A fanciful topper. Take a cue from the actress, who layered a shearling-trimmed Valentino jacket over a satin camisole, finishing with black high-vamp flats and stacks of jewelry for even more luxe detailing.

Baggy jeans are a signature in Rihanna’s wardrobe. For a dinner date in Paris, she dressed up Citizens of Humanity’s wide-leg silhouette with a black satin jacket for a chic evening look. Simply accessorize with Dior’s quilted Toujours bag, pointed black pumps, and a choker necklace for a desk-to-dinner pairing that works no matter where the day takes you.

Sienna Miller is keeping white jeans in rotation, even as the temperatures turn. The War actress was seen styling a frayed pair with an oversized navy sweater, red bomber jacket, and her favorite high-vamp black flats—an easy way to keep white denim going well into the colder months. Gucci’s Ophidia tote bag and a printed scarf make this feel especially on point for transitional dressing or as a polished travel outfit.

#6742. From Caramelized Amber to Bombshell Blowouts, These Are Fall’s Biggest Hair Trends

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Hairstylists share the buzziest fall hair trends their clients can’t get enough of.

When dried leaves in varying hues of orange, red, and yellow crunch under our feet, it’s basically a bat signal that the best season is underway. Fall sits right in the middle of summer’s balmy rays and winter’s biting chill, with a refreshing briskness that won’t necessarily expedite reversion for curly hair going straight and won’t dry out freshly bleached and/or dyed strands. The options are endless in this kind of weather, which can make decision-making feel a bit overwhelming. Do you try a new color? A bob cut? Maybe a pixie? According to the hottest hair trends of the season, you can do it all.

The transition from summer to fall is an important one for your hair. “Hair can be a little more compromised or porous based on the environment, from swimming pools and sun in the summer. Going from fall to winter, hair treatments to encourage hydration and strength are the easiest way to get your hair back on track,” says Eric Marshall Wright, stylist and owner of Eric Marshall Salon in Nashville, Tennessee. With a proper hair routine at home, your hair becomes strong enough to withstand your next hair transformation—that’s where fall’s biggest hair trends come in.

If you’re itching for a new hairdo, we polled several hairstylists, including Wright, to see what they predict will be the most head-turning hairstyles of the season, straight from their very own salons. Whether you’re a balayage connoisseur or tempted to do a bob, allow this list of trends to inspire you ahead of your next appointment.

Here’s a subtle take on the popular balayage technique that works with your hair color, creating a soft gradient with lowlights and highlights. “These highlights are soft, tone-on-tone highlights with dimension—think of them as a soft whisper in an overstimulated world. They look underdone instead of overdone; it’s a delicate hair color that’s sustainable and grounded. The look is effortlessly cool, glossy, and glazed for a finish that’s organically imperfect,” says Leslie Shores, color specialist at Eric Marshall Salon. This shade is perfect for “anyone who prefers a timeless, sustainable color. It’s achieved with no bleach, lightener, balayage, or ammonia-free demi-permanent hair color. Ask your colorist for soft tone-on-tone color.”

Sometimes the road to blonde is far too intimidating from dark brown or black. Shores’ answer to that gives you a lift without veering too much into blonde territory. “Cocoa brondette,” she says, is “a rich brunette with soft ribbons of deep indulgent brown shades.” The color is reminiscent of a rich cup of hot cocoa, with swirls of light brown throughout. “This shade looks best on someone with an olive skin tone, and can be achieved with demi-permanent or permanent hair color or with balayage. Ask your colorist for an all-over color with ammonia-free color around a level seven, six, or five; they can also paint soft ribbons of balayage.”

While most of the world is obsessed with bobs and pixies, another percentage of the population still favors long locks. Dimitris Giannetos, celebrity hairstylist and Great Lengths ambassador, says long hair isn’t going anywhere. “Hair can take a long minute to grow, so I have the help of Great Lengths, especially the Linea Wefts, to achieve the perfect, lived-in long hair,” he shares. His favorite hair trend this season? “CEO blowout,” which looks polished “but secure enough to get a bit messy.” This looks even better when paired with a “quiet, lived-in color, with more wispy, secret highlights versus an obvious balayage,” he adds. Your tools to achieve this are simple: “I use three different shades of the Great Lengths Line Wefts. They have such a fine spine, which makes them easy to blend and fully match your client’s color with an extra twist. They are super flat on the scalp, so they blend together perfectly without unwanted volume on the sides. I always recommend razoring the wefts at the end to create the perfect blend,” Giannetos says.

Wright concurs, adding that layers can elevate long styles that “looks effortless and moves.” Placement matters when it comes to layering hair, depending on the style you wear most often. “Layers can be as short as collarbone so you can easily put it up, but this is more about wearing it down and long-styled. Think hippie boho or 60s and long like Pocahontas. The cut is accomplished by point cutting and dry cutting techniques to make it soft and lived-in, not overly aggressive but effortless layers,” Wright shares.

If you want a louder balayage, Shores encourages you to opt for “rich shades of buttery gold and copper throughout the hair that look warm, rich, cozy, and earthy.” The gradient of hues might immediately scream summer, but it offers a toasted finish that “adds exotic warmth, depth, and dimension to the hair that feels like golden hour. Ask your colorist to paint big balayage pieces mainly in the front of the hair to match the volume and layers. These can be foiled or painted on. It looks best on brunettes and someone with thicker hair with layers.”

Already blonde? Shores suggests “bright, airy white-blonde balayage highlights that are airy and dreamy placed perfectly, as they carry a lightness to them that make them look ethereal and serene.” This look works great for those who are already “bright platinum without the constant touch up. [It’s also] perfect also for grey blending. This look can be achieved by using bleach balayage or foilyage. Ask your colorist to use bleach balayage or foilyage to get as light as possible!” she adds.

“Thanks to Off Campus and [actress] Ella Bright, we’re gravitating towards this shoulder-length bob that is worn flipped, sleek, curled, or blown out,” Wright says. Pictured here, this bob is marked by an asymmetrical blunt cut and soft waves throughout. “The cut needs to have facial shape and neck width taken into consideration, as those will cause different results, as well as the natural density and hair diameter,” Wright adds.

With summer’s sticky weather behind us, fall’s coolness means those bangs you’ve been dying to get won’t get too stuck to your forehead. “Being in a humid environment, they can devastate you in the summer, as the humidity makes them fussy. A fringe or bang can make you look styled and undone at the same time, meaning you can just style your bangs and pull your hair up to look chic. I recommend a fuller style rather than wispy so they look intentional. Keep hairline, cowlicks, and recession in mind, as bangs can have a mind of their own; style them first, as they can be difficult to dry on their own. For a softer, fuller look, ask your stylist to point-cut the ends for softness,” Wright explains.

Davines This is a Dry Texturizing Finishing Spray

“For long, high-volume natural textures, go with Davines Dry Texturize. This enhances volume on the mid-shaft through ends, especially for those who like texture and volume on their ends. Clipping [the hair] back [is an easy way] to give high volume to a half-up/half-down look and secure it with a claw clip.”—Eric Marshall Wright

“Those with sleek or textured bobs, I personally would recommend the Davines Shimmering Mist, as it creates high shine with zero hold. This could really emphasize the texture of the bob whether it’s straight or blown out or done with waves.”—EMW

Davines Hair Refresher, Dry Cleansing Shampoo

“As far as bangs go, I highly recommend the Davines Hair Refresher because bangs can be tricky and you sometimes need to rewash them. It’s nice to have something that is powder base to refresh them, that way you’re not re-styling them or rewetting them—you’re just refreshing them.”—EMW

Featuring a fall-ready leopard design, Wright loves these clips for tightly securing long hair in half-up, half-down styles.

#6740. All the Wardrobe Essentials Every Guy Should Own in 2026

When it comes to getting dressed, we often rhapsodize about the virtues of “wardrobe essentials for men” as if everyone knows what we mean. So, let's actually talk about it.

On Maslow's hierarchy of menswear needs, wardrobe essentials might begin the perfect white tee, a killer pair of jeans, and the shoes you can wear with them. But in compiling this list, our goal wasn’t simply to meet your needs—you are, frankly, a grown-ass man, and hopefully have those covered—but more to remind you of the fundamental pieces of menswear that have helped men look hotter and feel better for generations. And in a world of non-stop trends, we need these reminders now more than ever.

In aggregate, our essentials constitute the foundation of a rock-solid men’s basic wardrobe. Below, a highly specific starter pack of everything you’ll want—nay, need—to wear in the year of our lord 2026.

A plain white T-shirt can be worn as an undershirt, standalone with some vintage jeans, or—if you want to get DIY—screen-printed into a work of art. Looking for an indie version no one else has? Check out our guide to the best white tees.

Slim, abbreviated trunks or boxer briefs that keep everything in place are the foundation of every rock-solid wardrobe—whether other people can see ‘em or not. Even if you’re in the minority that’s committed to boxer shorts, it pays to spend a little more on something that’s, you know, holding your balls all day long.

We love the zany knitwear options flooding the internet these days. But if we're honest, there will always be a spot in our closets for a classic crewneck sweater. They're timeless and endlessly style-able, even if you only manage to drape one across your shoulders.

There's a reason that the Levi's 501s is at the very top of our guide to the best men's jeans: it has been, is, and always will be the jeans you come back to again (and again, and again). If you dig your denim light and a little looser, though, Gap's Loose Jeans are a close second. Can't think of what to wear? Here's your answer, seven days a week.

If there’s another theme here, it’s that menswear essentials shouldn’t be unitaskers. They should be useful in a variety of situations, and when it comes to tailoring in particular, the navy blazer is a Swiss Army Knife. It works in almost any situation, from job interviews (with a tie) to weddings (someone else's or your own). Bonus points if you opt for a double-breasted number with strong shoulders, brash peak lapels, and an unmistakable sense of what Italians—and menswear guys—call sprezzatura.

The menswear-sphere admittedly overloaded on loafers, and we’re now seeing a slight shift in the shoe zeitgeist. But that doesn’t take away from the fact that the right pair of loafers can still be the most versatile kicks in your closet. They’ve got more range than Daniel Day-Lewis and can go from casual to dressy to punk in a flash. Wear 'em with socks or without, and count yourself lucky when they get truly worn in—then keep wearing them.

Sure, everyone knows a guy who refuses to wear shorts. But he's overpowered every time by his greatest foes: Those months of the year where, honestly, wearing anything but a short becomes a compromise. Our favorite pairs merge style with practicality, and only look better the more thrashed they get. (Except for the Champion shorts—maybe keep those a little cleaner.)

They may have emerged from the sweaty, stylish world of sportswear, but hoodies have long since transcended their athletic origins. These ones have the stamina to take you from a coffee run to casual Friday at the office (just put it under one of those jean jackets we're always telling you about).

We get that simple sneakers aren’t exactly the type of kicks you lust after on StockX, but there’s no denying the rush of dopamine you get when you break out a fresh pair, or how well they go with literally everything. At less than a Benjamin there's the Converse Chuck Taylor, a mainstay of our sneakers coverage, since, uh, always.

Not ready to take the plunge on a serious diver from Rolex or Omega? You're in luck: Seiko's much-heralded 5 series gives you everything you could want in a dive watch—an automatic movement, a day-date display, water resistance, and a near-indestructible case—at a price that won't require a second mortgage. (If you've got a few more dollars to play around with, Hamilton is no slouch, either.)

Like a plain white tee or simple white crew socks, a white Oxford shirt is a true workhorse. It can take the 9-to-5 like a champ, sharpen up for a fancier occasion, or kick back wide open over your favorite vintage tee. If you only have one shirt with buttons, let it be this.

Remember chinos? The wardrobe staple of preppies and, inexplicably, grandpas everywhere? The pant that taps in when your jeans need a break? The ones that Gap viral-ized in the late-90s? These days chinos are back and bigger than before. The chinos of today are surprisingly familiar and look more like the military-issued pairs of the midcentury—high rise and hella roomy. Some even have a pleat or two. We're all for going wide and pleated, but these both present a happy-ish medium.

While people usually start talking about them in April, sunglasses are a year-round necessity—overcast January skies be damned. They’re relevant whether you’re soaking up the summer rays, trying to cut the wintry glare, or simply trying to navigate life with a little more stealth.

Headwear trends come and go—we see you, crochet knit beanies and Trucker hats—but the baseball cap is eternal. You wear one, your dad wears one, your grandpa wears one. The solution for everything from a bad hair day, to an impromptu work Zoom, to forgetting to pack your sunglasses, they're also just plain cool, whether brand new or a little worn out. Always have been, always will.

Sweatpants should be cozy, sure, but the best of the genre are so much more than mere lazy-Sunday garb. We’ve moved past the calf-gripping elastane-pumped versions that have defined the closets of so many Lulu bros and dudes who have skate decks hung up as art. Instead, sweatpants now should be closer to the originals with a baggier fit and even wide-open hems. Spring for a pair that oozes Rocky-level charm, and they'll become the bed-to-bodega bottoms you can't stop wearing outside of the house, too.

There were a few years where the collective menswear consciousness leaned into “fun socks,” and further away from God. How easily we are led astray… Thankfully, we all now agree that the best socks are really the ones you forget that you're wearing, because they're so quietly consistent and comfortable. And in all of our years of reporting on savvy men's style choices, we've never heard a bad word said against any of the four contenders below.

Sometimes clothes can make you feel like you’re living a movie, and a good trench coat is like you’re aiming for an Oscar. (Those trucker jackets with the sewn-in hoodie are more like Hallmark). It’s the most dramatic garment you can have in your closet, and while wooden top coats are great when it's freezing out, a lighter-weight trench coat works the other nine months of the year—and can be paired with a heavy sweater for the other three. You may not be starring in any blockbusters coming up soon, but, boy, will you look like you're ready to.

In cooler temperatures, a reliable flannel shirt is more than a wardrobe essential: it's a no-brainer. Most versions will be plaid, but all of them should feel substantial enough to double as a light jacket, thanks to their lightweight wool or thick cotton make.

It's hard to think of a jacket more useful, more handsome, more versatile—heck, more all three at once—than the canvas jacket. These days, the original designs still retains their utilitarian charm, but the hammer and nails that used to accompany them have long since been replaced by a cell phone and ear buds. And thanks to fashion's ongoing workwear fixation, there's never been a wider range of luxe designer versions available.

Black derbies can pull through when you need shoes for more formal occasions—and also elevate a quick-and-dirty jeans-and-tee outfit. Dr. Martens are a great entry-level choice, and you'll get a lot more mileage out of the Mono pair, which forgoes the brand's signature yellow stitching for discreet black thread.

When your dress pants are this good—roomy and comfortable, statement-making but versatile—there's no sense in saving them for special occasions. Wear them all the time, with anything, the way you would your jeans.

Belts are often an afterthought, but they really shouldn't be. So don't waist (sorry) the opportunity. Much like cowboy boots, the western belt is riding high in fashion right now—but for this story's purposes, we'd like to guide you back to more classic styles, even if the two belts up top have a certain western flair.

By now, you're probably getting the idea that the name of the game here is versatility. While you could opt for Chelsea boots—the right pair will be able to withstand the elements, and any sideways glances from your office nemesis—you'll feel so much calmer in a pair truly designed to stomping through snowy slush.

We love that iconic North Face puffer as much as the next guy (you know the one we're talking about). But don't let its objectively perfect design distract you from the avalanche of stellar, lesser-known alternatives on the market.

A good duffel bag needs to do only one thing: hold stuff. A great duffel bag, though, needs to check off a few more boxes. It should still carry your clothes, kicks, chargers, toiletries, and everything else in the most space-efficient, easy-to-find way possible. But it should also be designed to outlast your passport—or better yet, you—despite years of being stuffed in an overhead bin and thrown in the trunk of your car. We've tested hundreds of 'em over the years, and the ones below offer all that and more.

#6737. Salma Hayek Pinault, Jane Fonda, and Hollywood’s Leading Names Gathered to Toast Women In Film

If there was one room in Hollywood where female power was unmistakable, it was the Beverly Hilton on Thursday night, where Women In Film hosted its annual WIF Honors. Since 1977, the organization has honored some of the entertainment industry’s most accomplished names, celebrating their contributions to film and television, and this time around was no exception.

Presented in partnership with Max Mara, the night brought together Salma Hayek Pinault, Kerry Washington, Jane Fonda, Olivia Munn, Emmy Rossum, Sharon Stone, and Katherine LaNasa. Naturally, Max Mara had plenty of representation in the room, with Fonda, Hannah Waddingham, Caylee Cowan, and breakthrough star Adria Arjona among those wearing the Italian label. Washington, meanwhile, opted for Balmain, while LaNasa chose Michael Kors.

One of the night’s standout moments came when Fonda took the stage to present Hayek Pinault with the Jane Fonda Humanitarian Award. It was a particularly fitting pairing, given their longstanding commitment to using their platforms to advocate for human rights and social issues. Reflecting on their shared history, Fonda recalled traveling to Mexico with Hayek Pinault more than two decades ago to raise awareness about hundreds of women and girls who had been murdered or declared missing.

What stood out to Fonda then, and since, is Hayek Pinault’s unwavering dedication to the causes she takes on. “She’s so passionate, and what really impressed me is how she listens to people and really gets to know them,” Fonda told the audience. “You can’t just write a check, you have to be there and have kinship.”

Fonda also praised Hayek Pinault’s efforts to end systemic violence against women and girls, including her testimony before the U.S. Senate and her work through the Kering Foundation. “She understands power. We all need to understand power and learn how to wield it,” Fonda said, before delivering a final tribute. “This is a woman who knows that getting what you want often requires more than good intentions. It requires guts, being prepared to get in the ring and fight, and boy, has she fought. And the willingness to get your hands dirty.”

Dressed in Bottega Veneta, Hayek Pinault accepted the honor from her longtime friend and mentor. Rather than deliver a traditional acceptance speech, the actress settled in for an onstage conversation with Fonda that offered a glimpse into what drives her philanthropy and activism.

As for her desire to bring more authentic Hispanic characters and stories to international audiences, Hayek Pinault explained that producing became her way of creating the path she felt was missing when she first arrived in Hollywood. “I complained a lot about the lack of opportunities when I arrived here, so the only way I could do something about it was [getting] behind the camera,” she said. “I created a company that created opportunities for others.” Noting that nearly all the projects her company has produced have not featured her, she added, “It’s for other people. To tell our stories, I don’t have to be center stage.”

When the conversation turned to her work with her husband François-Henri Pinault through the Kering Foundation, she summed up the motivation behind their efforts in one word: “Love. Really, it is love. I do it with my love. I found myself a partner who respects what I do. It’s wonderful to have a man that cares about women. We do it together.”

On the red carpet, Hayek Pinault offered another glimpse into the determination that has shaped her career. “They told me to go back to my country. ‘There’s no opportunities here. You’re a big star in Mexico, go back. Don’t be silly,’” she recalled to Vogue. “They meant well, by the way.”

But even back then, Hayek Pinault trusted her instincts and saw an audience that the American entertainment industry hadn’t yet figured out how to reach. “There are 42 million Latinos in this country, and [Hollywood] literally didn’t understand it. I knew it would happen. I just didn’t know it would happen in my time.”

Hayek Pinault was among several honorees recognized throughout the evening. The WIF Max Mara Face of the Future Award went to Arjona, who’s readying to appear in next year’s hotly anticipated The Thomas Crown Affair. The Puerto Rico-born emerging talent was also fêted the night before the WIF Honors by the fashion label at a chic cocktail reception at Chateau Marmont.

Pamela Abdy, former co-chair and co-CEO of Warner Bros. Motion Picture Group, received the inaugural Vanguard Award, celebrating a career dedicated to moving the industry forward. Filmmaker Beth de Araújo and actress Gemma Chan shared the Crystal Award for Advocacy in Film for their work on Josephine, the psychological drama that made a splash at the Sundance Film Festival.

Waddingham, meanwhile, was presented with the Crystal Award for Advocacy in TV, recognizing the Emmy-winning Ted Lasso star’s commitment to creating more opportunities for women both in front of and behind the camera. And if anyone was expecting a subdued acceptance speech, Waddingham had another thing in mind. “Being in this room tonight is like the most concentrated, potent shot in the arm of every single podcast I would ever want to listen to in one hit,” she began, drawing laughs from the audience. “To even be here and share time and oxygen and a cheeky beverage or two with you all—I mean, it’s just f*cking great!”

But beneath the humor was a serious message. “I take the status, the platform, and the voice that I have been afforded incredibly seriously,” she said, reflecting on her commitment to speaking up for others, from the LGBTQ+ community to women fighting for better access in the industry. “As long as there is breath in my body, I will stand on that ladder with my incredibly high, fabulous heels. On the bottom rung, I will always give a hand to those who need it. I encourage you to do the same because the soul is so rewarding when advocating for others, and it is endless,” she concluded.

#6736. ELLE Escapes: Palm Beach

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

There’s just something about Palm Beach. Maybe it’s the namesake trees, the prime people-watching, or the air of exclusivity that comes with its private beaches and members-only clubs. Whatever the draw, this laid-back island feels more desirable than ever, even if a presidential visit to Mar-a-Lago means contending with a little extra gridlock. Roll down the windows, leave reality behind, and settle into one of Florida’s most rarefied corners for a weekend of luxury, indulgence, and enviable living. Ahead, I’ve rounded up where the well-heeled snowbirds eat, drink, and shop on their next trip down south.

With shops like Zimmermann, Hermès, and Veronica Beard, a tempting lineup of restaurants, and even a gelato stand at Sant Ambreous, the John Volk-designed Royal Poinciana Plaza is more than enough to fill an afternoon, and you’ll be happy to let it.

Golf and Palm Beach go hand in hand. If you’re a novice like me, this scenic par-3 course overlooking the water is the ideal place to work on your swing—or relive those regrettable bogeys long after you’ve left the green.

Step into the spa at Eau Resort & Spa, and it’s immediately clear why it earned a place in the hotel’s name. From the impeccable service and indulgent treatments to the top-tier facilities, the sprawling 42,000-square-foot space is the ultimate place for a little (or a lot of) pampering.

Lack of Color Utopia Inca Raffia Bucket Hat

Does it get any better than Nobu? From its signature miso black cod and rock shrimp tempura to the yellowtail jalapeño and specialty rolls, every dish is a standout. Add impeccable presentation to the mix, and this Japanese-Peruvian favorite never disappoints. Its new location at the Eau is no exception.

Set on the picturesque terrace of The Brazilian Court Hotel, this much-talked-about Daniel Boulud-helmed restaurant lives up to the hype. You really can’t go wrong with anything on the menu, but the White Cosmo (a mix of vodka, elderflower, and white cranberry, finished with an orchid ice cube) is begging to be Instagrammed.

For the uninitiated, the Nora (North of the Railroad) District in West Palm Beach is quickly becoming the city’s next big thing, and Del Mar is helping lead the charge. Steps away from the newly opened Nora Hotel, its Mediterranean-inspired menu and sprawling 12,000-square-foot space, complete with a 100-seat courtyard, feel both inviting and refined. Don’t miss the Open Fire Roasted Shellfish Tower, made for sharing (though I won’t judge if you keep it all to yourself).

Farm Rio Golden Yellow Anthurium Square Neck Mini Dress

Alexis Bittar Liquid Lucite Front Back Hoop Earring

Andrea Gomez Bella Raffia Platform Sandals

Open for breakfast, lunch, or dinner, Swifty’s, the poolside restaurant at The Colony Hotel, proves that casual dining can still deliver. Stick around for the live music, particularly the acoustic guitarists who stick to the hits (no requests necessary). And before you call it a day, make a pit-stop at the pool-deck newsstand to pick up the latest issue of ELLE.

HMF, the restaurant and lounge at The Breakers, is a great spot for a pre-dinner drink before wandering the resort’s storied halls. And its wine credentials are nothing short of legendary: It’s earned a Grand Award from Wine Spectator every year since the awards program began in 1981.

Just a block from the ocean, this picturesque, pink-hued property packs plenty into its 79 rooms, including a sunset-facing pool deck, a gym, a ballroom, and, of course, a stunning bar.

Coniglio Palm Beach Cinch Back Silk Midi Skirt

Tucked away on Lake Mangonia in West Palm Beach, the Belgrove Resort & Spa has all the makings of a perfect getaway. Think an 18-hole golf course, four tennis courts, two pickleball courts, two padel courts, private balconies in every guest room, a gym, a spa, three pools, and two hot tubs. Whether you’re after an action-packed escape or some serious R&R, you’ll find it here. And when you’re ready to venture out, a complimentary shuttle will take you anywhere within a five-mile radius.

Sizable suites? Check. A private, shaded pool and on-site hair salon? Check. Custom Linus bikes to borrow and complimentary yacht rides? Absolutely. The Brazilian Court Hotel feels like a true home base in the heart of town, just a quick ride from the Palm Beach Lake Trail. As owner Courtney Schlesinger puts it: “The hotel was built to feel like a private estate, so when you’re here, you feel like you have your own place in Palm Beach. That’s what I love the most: waking up in the morning, sitting on the terrace with a coffee, and imagining Daniel Boulud is my own private chef.”

A little off the beaten path and about a 20-minute drive from Palm Beach, Eau Resort & Spa more than makes up for its location with direct beach access, guest rooms designed by Jonathan Adler, two pools, a world-class spa, and a full-service beauty salon offering manicures, pedicures, and blowouts. Add six restaurants (including Nobu) and kid-friendly perks like childcare and an arcade, and you have everything you need for a getaway without ever leaving the property. So why would you?

The Row Ginza Leather and Suede Platform Flip Flops

For a face that gleams in the sunlight, pack this hydrating oil with vitamin C in your beach bag.

L’Oréal Paris Voluminous Lash Paradise Waterproof Mascara

If you plan jumping in the pool, applying waterproof mascara is a must. Sweat- and water-resistant with a lengthening effect, this one pairs well with a cocktail.

Shiseido Urban Environment Oil-Free Sunscreen SPF 42

#6735. Rosie Huntington-Whiteley Goes Completely Backless in a Sculptural Gucci Dress

She made a statement at the 2026 LACMA Gala

At the 2026 LACMA Art+Film Gala, Rosie Huntington-Whiteley was all business in the front, party in the back. Showing up to the Los Angeles County Museum of Art’s annual black-tie event—where everyone from philanthropists to actors to musicians to athletes came together for a glamorous evening of fundraising—the model was seen wearing a sleek black dress with a surprise.

Courtesy of Gucci, the evening’s sponsor, the piece appeared simple and modest at first glance—with a front defined by a sculptural, exaggerated high neckline and a slim-fit long-sleeve, floor-length silhouette. When Huntington-Whiteley turned, however, the dress was revealed to be (almost) entirely open, with a singular piece of silver hardware creating separation between a low scoop back and a high leg slit.

And, if that wasn’t enough, the whole garment was lined with dark-green sequins, which shimmered subtly in the light. She matched the shade to her diamond-and emerald earrings, which were on full display thanks to her slicked-back ponytail. She slipped into pointed-toe black pumps and stopped for photos in front of Chris Burden’s famed public art installation, Urban Light, which doubled as a red carpet for the evening.

The Art+Film Gala celebrated its 15th year tonight, supporting the museum’s ongoing efforts to expand its film programming. It honored the work of painter Vija Celmins, known for her photo-realistic work exploring the complexity of nature, as well as Dune filmmaker Denis Villeneuve. Blackpink’s Rosé was tapped for a musical performance, and, like every year, Leonardo DiCaprio and LACMA trustee Eva Chow served as co-chairs.

Consider this week’s edit your guide to everything from transitional fall looks to clever layering techniques, all infused with plenty of off-duty flair.

This week, celebrities embraced the seasonal chill, stepping out in their fall outerwear best. Naomi Watts chose a double-breasted pinstripe blazer over a crisp white T-shirt and relaxed denim, finishing the look with playful accessories, including a floral brooch, an oversized-buckle belt, and a printed silk scarf. Meanwhile, guests at the CFDA Awards in New York offered a glimpse of what’s to come for occasion dressing as the holiday season approaches. Alexa Chung arrived in Tory Burch’s velvet robe dress and leather pumps in mustard tones, accessorizing with Elsa Peretti for Tiffany & Co. jewelry for a decadent finish. Gold is having a moment, and there's no better time to embrace a little evening opulence for upcoming weddings, cocktail events, or festive celebrations.

Minimalist mule sandals, a sleek clutch, and diamond drop earrings keep things firmly in evening territory, while her ball cap offers an easy day-to-night switch-up.
